Kuṭaru is, according to the commentator Mahīdhara, synonymous with kukkuṭa, ‘cock.’ The word is found in the yajurveda Saṃhitās only.
Foot notes On Vājasaneyi Saṃhitā, xxiv, 23.
taittirīya Saṃhitā, v. 5, 17, 1; Maitrāyaṇī Saṃhitā, i. 1, 6; iii. 14, 4. 20; iv. 1, 6; Vājasaneyi Saṃhitā, xxiv. 23, 39.
Cf. Zimmer, Altindisches Leben, 93.

Kūṭa, a word found in the Rigveda, the Atharvaveda, and the Brāhmaṇas, is of doubtful signification. On the whole, the most probable sense is hammer, which suits every passage adequately. The St. Petersburg Dictionary renders it ‘horn,’ which is the sense accepted by Whitney for the Atharvaveda passage where it occurs. Geldner thinks that it means ‘trap.’
